title: Tethered rollback checklist and warm-priming lab
body:
Purpose: quick personal playbook for tethered rollback flows + warm priming. Mostly notes-to-self for next oncall/ship day. Keep lightweight, actionable, and focused on observable signals we can use without asking infra.

Context and motivation:
- We often need to flip models or pin versions for a small cohort but retain a fast escape hatch when hallucinations/backwards regressions happen.
- Tethered rollback: keep the routing decision tied to an external allowlist (cohort IDs) or a token bucket that we can close instantly.
- Warm priming: before moving traffic, ensure KV cache/prefix cache and prompt warmup to avoid early latency spikes and first-token regression.

Quick TL;DR checklist (short actionable items):
1) Preflight (30–90m before cohort start)
   - Verify model binaries and quantization variant uploaded (S3 / model-registry) and sha matches release notes.
   - Run smoke-gen locally: 10 requests with representative prompt set; note latency and token distributions.
   - Warm cache: run prefix batch for top 20 high-frequency prompts (use /tools/warmup-script). Capture average first-token time.
   - Create tether in routing config (temp flag: reroute.gate.<release-id> = "tethered")
   - Create rollback flag in feature-flags (FF): ff/release-<id>-kill = off

2) Canary (minutes -> hours depending on risk)
   - Start with 0.5% global or 1% of target tenant segments.
   - Observe: error_rate (5xx), avg latency P95, downstream user error signals (client-reports slack channel #release-monitor), quality metric (BLEU/SIM or task-specific evals if available).
   - If any of: error_rate > baseline + 3x, P95 latency > baseline + 200ms, quality delta < -6% (or absolute QA failing cases > 5), then immediately set feature-flag ff/release-<id>-kill = on -> automatic fallback.
   - Keep open a rollback issue in INF triage (INF-<temp-idx>) and annotate with timestamps of decision.

3) Unpin / expand
   - If stable after 2h for small cohorts, scale to 5% then monitor for 6h window before broader ramp.
   - Use gradual pin-down windows (e.g., 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with manual go/no-go checkpoints.

Tether semantics and fast escape:
- Tethered routing uses a single boolean in the routing-layer combined with cohort allowlist. This allows "close tether" to cut traffic instantly.
- Implementation notes: 'close tether' flips routing rule to always route to fallback model variant; confirm via routing-sim endpoint (POST /tools/sim-route).
- If the routing-layer suffers, the secondary escape is the feature flag at the client SDK (force-fallback) — inform SDK owners if this is likely to be used.

Warm-priming specifics (practical):
- Priming set = top n prompts by qps for the last 7 days for the tenants in the cohort. Default n = 30.
- Run warmup with sequence length typical to workload rather than max. This avoids cache pollution and ensures kernel paths are exercised.
- Scripts: /infra/scripts/warmup_kv.py --model <id> --cohort <label> --samples 30
- Timeline: warmup 15–30m before enabling routing; re-run warmup after each major scale step.

Telemetry signals to watch (immediate):
- request.latency.first_token_ms (P50/P95) — sudden increase indicates cache miss or serving path change
- request.errors.5xx.rate and request.errors.model_decode_failures
- model.output.quality.<eval-set>.delta (if available inline) — we need quick lightweight eval harness hooked into CI
- deployment.traffic_split.by_cohort (ensure traffic is hitting intended cohort)
- business KPIs: CTR/accept-rate/drop-rate on a rolling window — sometimes the app-level signal is faster than model metrics

Rollback garden-paths (escalation ladder):
1) Flip tether -> fallback model
2) Toggle SDK feature-flag (client-side fallback)
3) Revert routing config to pinned-old-model version
4) Re-deploy previous model binary (if route-level pin is not sufficient)
5) If catastrophic, open binary-redeploy incident and coordinate with SRE for capacity throttles

Common gotchas and reminders:
- TTLs: confirm cache TTL on KV store matches the warmup expectations (we saw a 10m TTL once and warmup was useless)
- Warmup size: too many warm requests for large cohorts can spike token cost; coordinate with finance if > 50k tokens anticipated.
- Region affinity: if cohort is region-anchored, warmup must run in same region to populate local caches.
- Quant variants: metric drift often comes from different quantization knobs, not the model weights. Keep a table of quant variants tested.

Open questions / TODO (for follow-up):
- Can we get a "rapid-eval" webhook to post 10-sample quality check directly into the release slack thread? (Ping @devex)
- Should we wire a synthetic client-side canary that fuzzes prompts to catch hallucination types earlier?
- Need a lightweight charge-estimate before warmups run — short script or tile in console (cost in tokens + estimated $)
- Consider template: "tethered-rollout-play" in Confluence for cross-team runbook. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/tethered-rollouts (WIP)

Notes to self (handy commands):
- warmup: infra/scripts/warmup_kv.py --model rwd-v2-small --cohort alpha --samples 30
- simulate routing: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/sim-route -d '{"cohort":"alpha","model":"rwd-v2-small"}'
- flip tether: infra/ops/feature_flags set ff/release-ALPHA-kill true
- check traffic: graphql query deploymentTraffic(releaseId: "ALPHA") { byCohort }

Postmortem skeleton (if rollback triggered):
- timeline: minute granularity starting T-60m
- signals: metrics + logs + user reports
- root cause hypothesis: (quantization / cache / kernel mismatch / prompt-sensitive regression)
- immediate remediations taken
- long-term actions (tests to add, monitoring to improve)

Housekeeping: leave a single line note in the release thread with the timestamp when tether was opened/closed; keep ownership on-call person in the subject line.

Personal heuristics (when to abort quickly):
- When model hallucination causes user-visible P0 errors (e.g., policy-violating content) — immediate kill.
- When P95 latency regresses >300ms and recovery not within 10 minutes after warmup re-run.
- When failures are correlated to a single customer/tenant with high churn risk — prefer targeted unpin over global rollback.

Endnotes:
- This is a working scratchpad. Clean up into a proper playbook once we've validated the failure signals in INF-2347.
- If I use this in a real deploy, leave a brief note at the top: "used on YYYY-MM-DD by <owner> — outcome: <ok/fallback/rollback>"
